SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: AUDIENCE SPEAKING 1/
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Audience SPEAKING 1/ helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: AUDIENCE SPEAKING 1/
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

In this part you learn to Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

1. Read the idea carefully: Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when.

PART 2: Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Audience SPEAKING 1/ to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Audience SPEAKING 1/ is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Audience SPEAKING 1/”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Audience SPEAKING 1/ to a partner. (skill: Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Audience SPEAKING 1/ to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when.
3. Practise this skill: Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Audience SPEAKING 1/ from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Audience SPEAKING 1/: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Audience SPEAKING 1/?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How should I speak to be SPEAKING awareness learners should be able to: listen to recorded pieces of their heard?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Audience SPEAKING 1/ means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Speak clearly when talking own voice. 2. What should I do to make to others in and out of class. • Learners could be encouraged to myself clear e.g when.
5. Be able to: Demonstrate ability to speak conversations whenever confidently in and out of opportunities arise. class. • In pairs and small groups.
